analysis.title: Santa Rally Now, Price Resets Later: Is Goldman's Year-End Squeeze Call Just The Latest Consensus Trade To Fade?
key_insights: Goldman's Macro Roadmap (Cosimo Codacci-Pisanelli, Rikin Shah) sees conditions for equities to squeeze higher into year-end. The reasons given are the recent equity sell-off, lower multiples, much lighter positioning and supportive seasonals.

Goldman describes deleveraging into the lows as extreme. Net/gross de-risking in its US prime book was one of the most aggressive episodes of the past decade, and Thursday's Nasdaq sell-off was a ~5 sigma move.

Morgan Stanley's prime brokerage found hedge funds underweight AI for the first time since 2023, in the largest sustained stretch of L/S de-risking in over 15 years. MS also flagged a record 70% tech momentum crash, and JPMorgan told clients to buy.

Goldman says the market absorbed a stronger CPI print, hawkish Fed comments, a rate sell-off, an oil rally and Nvidia news flow in one week. It reads this as evidence of a supportive market structure.
Valuation leg: MSCI AC World 12-month forward P/E is 15.6x and PEG is 1.1x, both near their averages since 1997. Consensus EPS for 2026, 2027 and especially 2028 has been revised up.
S&P 500 forward P/E is 17.9x with the 10Y real rate at 2.25%. Goldman's regression implies about 18.9x, so the S&P trades roughly one turn below where real rates alone would put it.

Goldman is less concerned by AI supply constraints (capital, permitting, energy) than by demand or monetization risk. It calls the 2y picture for the AI complex very unclear, and the demand verdict comes with Q4 earnings, with limited new information until then.

Inflation has not gone away. US CPI beat in both September and October on a broad basis, and producer and import price inflation have accelerated. Global manufactured goods import price inflation is above pandemic-era rates.

The breadth of price pressure has widened into chemicals, plastics and paper products. The share of import price categories running above a 5% annualized pace is roughly 25-40% in the US, Germany, France, Italy and the UK, and above 40% for US producer price categories.

Goldman says upstream price increases can take 6-12 months to pass through to consumer prices. It calls Q1 the real test, with a January effect when many price components reset at once, about 16 components with a 2-sigma reset in January against about 2.5 or fewer in other months.
Goldman economists added a third rate hike to their forecast after the CPI report. The desk recommends being long front-end inflation, citing risk of higher inflation surprises through Q1.

Rates idea: the long end of the European curve is rich, with EUR 20y10y the only point across G4 curves richer than before the Iran crisis began in February. EUR 10s30s at -13bp looks too flat vs Goldman's fair-value model, and steepener positioning is extremely light ahead of the January Dutch pension reform.
Goldman suggests pairing European curve steepeners with a front-end beta hedge or long front-end inflation, or being short the forwards. Named risks are energy and the January price resets.

UK: the BoE hiked and guided to one more move without timing, which Goldman calls muddled messaging. It argues the 4.9% Q2 inflation peak forecast skews risks dovishly and likes receiving the December and February meetings, while keeping UK longs strictly at the very front end.

Goldman's summary says 2026 has been a horrible year for macro markets, where fading every consensus trade has been the playbook. It warns that a strong equity squeeze would make duration harder, especially if January inflation prints are strong.

The article's author argues the year-end squeeze is itself becoming a consensus trade, citing JPM (capitulation far along), Morgan Stanley (deep fear) and Goldman. It sees the post-Christmas inflation bill as the more durable part of the note.
This morning's PPI headline was a tenth softer than expected at 0.3% MoM (6.5% YoY), but intermediate PPI is running at more than double final demand.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman says the 2y picture for the AI complex is very unclear. It is more worried about demand or monetization risk than supply constraints, and the demand verdict comes with Q4 earnings.

earnings_insights: Goldman says the demand-side verdict for the AI build-out comes with Q4 earnings, and incremental information before then will remain limited.
Consensus EPS estimates for 2026, 2027 and especially 2028 have been revised up, which the article contrasts with the usual pattern of slow cuts (consensus estimates, not reported figures).

Companies have absorbed a large portion of input cost increases in their margins per Goldman. The open question is how long that lasts, and if demand cannot absorb it, the labour market may take some of the hit.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman economists now see more tightening, in line with the January inflation reset thesis.

risk_factors: Q1 inflation: January price resets and 6-12 month pass-through of upstream costs could add upward pressure to consumer prices.
A year-end equity squeeze could ease financial conditions and remove the growth downside tails that kept central banks patient, making duration harder.
AI demand or monetization risk, to be tested by Q4 earnings.
Energy prices, a named risk to the European steepener.
If demand cannot absorb input costs, the labour market may take some of the heat as margin absorption ends.
The year-end squeeze may be a crowded consensus trade, since JPM, Morgan Stanley and Goldman all lean the same way.

Scatter of S&P forward P/E against the 10Y real rate, latest point 17.9x at a 2.25% real rate vs about 18.9x on the regression line.
Forward curve chart since February 27: US, UK and Japanese forwards up 30bps to 165bps while EUR 20y10y is down more than 10bps.
Count of price components with 2-sigma resets by month, with January at roughly 16 vs roughly 2.5 or fewer in other months.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman's US prime book saw one of the most aggressive net/gross de-risking episodes of the past decade, and positioning is now much lighter.
Morgan Stanley's prime brokerage found hedge funds underweight AI for the first time since 2023, the largest sustained L/S de-risking in over 15 years.
Curve steepeners were the epicentre of the deleveraging through September in Europe, leaving positioning extremely light ahead of the January Dutch pension reform.
Thursday's Nasdaq sell-off was a ~5 sigma move per Goldman.
geopolitical: The Iran crisis began in February 2026. Since February 27 US, UK and Japanese forward curves have sold off by 30bps to 165bps, while EUR 20y10y is lower.
The 2026 energy shock is cited as the source of the inflation bill expected to arrive in Q1.
cross_bank_references: JPM has called capitulation far along and mapped out who could be forced to buy.
Morgan Stanley has catalogued the deep fear and found hedge funds underweight AI for the first time since 2023.
JPMorgan told clients to buy on Tuesday, and Mark Schilsky judged the vibes pretty terrible (which should be Bullish!).

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman cites extreme de-grossing, MSCI P/Es back at 35-year averages, upward EPS revisions and supportive seasonals, so equities can squeeze higher into December.
tension_points.bear_case: The squeeze is becoming a consensus trade, and a rally that eases financial conditions could remove the reason for central banks to stay patient, raising inflation and duration risk in Q1.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Q4 earnings showing AI demand or monetization at risk, or a strong January effect in Q1 inflation prints.

tension_points.bull_case: The European long end is rich vs the fair-value model, steepener positioning is extremely light and the January Dutch pension reform could have a larger market impact.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy prices and January price resets could hurt the position, so Goldman suggests a front-end beta hedge or long front-end inflation.
